formalDefinition: A mathematical characterization of algorithm efficiency describing the limiting behavior of execution time or memory footprint as input size approaches infinity.
eli5: A way to measure how much slower a program gets when you give it ten, a thousand, or a million times more data to process.
analogy: Finding a friend in a room of 10 people takes seconds (O(N)); looking up a name in an alphabetical phonebook takes a few flips regardless of size (O(log N)).
keyTakeaway: Helps engineers choose the right algorithm before writing heavy production code.

formalDefinition: An attention mechanism relating different positions of a single sequence in order to compute a contextualized representation of the sequence via query, key, and value vectors.
eli5: When reading a sentence, your brain connects 'it' back to the noun mentioned three words ago. Self-attention lets computers do the same thing across an entire document.
analogy: Highlighting related clues with different colored markers on a detective board so every word knows who its friends are.
keyTakeaway: The core architectural innovation behind modern Large Language Models (LLMs).

formalDefinition: A fundamental conjecture in distributed data stores stating that it is impossible to simultaneously provide more than two out of three guarantees: Consistency, Availability, and Partition Tolerance.
eli5: In a distributed network where cables might get cut, you must choose between always showing the newest data (Consistency) or always answering immediately even with slightly old data (Availability).
analogy: If the phone line between two bank branches drops, they can either stop withdrawals (safe consistency) or keep handing out cash risking an overdraft (high availability).
keyTakeaway: Guides architecture decisions when building global scale databases.

formalDefinition: A first-order iterative optimization algorithm for finding a local minimum of a differentiable objective function by taking steps proportional to the negative of the gradient.
eli5: A method for an AI to learn by making small adjustments to its guesses, getting a little less wrong each time.
analogy: Walking down a foggy mountain by feeling which direction slopes downward with your feet until you reach the lowest valley.
keyTakeaway: The primary engine used to train neural networks and machine learning models.

formalDefinition: A state in concurrent programming where two or more processes are unable to proceed because each is waiting for the other to release a mutually acquired resource.
eli5: A traffic gridlock where car A waits for car B to move, but car B is waiting for car A to move, so nobody can go.
analogy: Two people meeting in a narrow doorway, each refusing to step back until the other steps forward first.
keyTakeaway: Prevented using strict lock ordering, timeouts, or lock-free data structures.

formalDefinition: Mathematical representations of unstructured data (text, images, audio) mapped into continuous, high-dimensional vector spaces where semantic similarity correlates with geometric distance.
eli5: Converting words and thoughts into lists of coordinates on a map so that words with similar meanings live in the same neighborhood.
analogy: Organizing spices in a pantry: sweet spices on one shelf, spicy peppers on another, so similar flavors are always close together.
keyTakeaway: Power semantic search, recommendation engines, and RAG architectures in modern AI.

formalDefinition: A self-balancing tree data structure that maintains sorted data and allows searches, sequential access, insertions, and deletions in logarithmic amortized time, optimized for block storage.
eli5: An organized filing cabinet system where each drawer has labels pointing to narrower sections, letting you find any record in 3 quick steps.
analogy: An airport terminal directory that tells you first which concourse, then which gate group, then the exact gate.
keyTakeaway: The backbone indexing mechanism inside PostgreSQL, MySQL, and traditional relational databases.

formalDefinition: The property of a computational system or instruction set that enables it to simulate any single-taped Universal Turing Machine, given sufficient time and storage.
eli5: If a programming language can simulate any calculation or program that any computer could ever theoretically run, it's Turing Complete.
analogy: A Lego set with enough basic bricks to build any sculpture or mechanism you can imagine.
keyTakeaway: Almost all modern languages (Python, JS, C++) are Turing Complete, while config formats (JSON) are intentionally not.

formalDefinition: A cryptographic protocol by which one party (the prover) can prove to another party (the verifier) that a given statement is true without revealing any information apart from the fact that the statement is indeed true.
eli5: Proving to someone that you know a secret password or that you are over 18 without ever showing them the password or your ID card.
analogy: Proving to a colorblind friend that two balls are different colors: you hold one in each hand, hide them behind your back, and let your friend guess if you swapped them—after 20 rounds, they know you can tell the colors apart without ever knowing which ball is red or green.
keyTakeaway: Powers privacy-preserving authentication, blockchain scaling, and secure identity verification.

formalDefinition: A cryptographic system that uses pairs of mathematically related keys: a public key for encryption or signature verification, and a private key kept secret for decryption or signing.
eli5: Using one key to lock a mailbox so anyone can drop a letter in, and a completely different secret key that only you have to open the mailbox and read the letters.
analogy: A padlock you hand out unlocked to everyone in town (public key): anyone can snap it shut on a box and mail it to you, but only your unique physical key (private key) can unlock it.
keyTakeaway: The foundation of HTTPS, SSH, and secure communication over the open internet.

formalDefinition: A deterministic mathematical algorithm that maps data of arbitrary size to a fixed-size bit array (hash digest) in a one-way manner that is computationally infeasible to invert.
eli5: A digital blender that turns any file or password into a unique fixed-length fingerprint—you can easily make the fingerprint, but you can never reconstruct the original ingredients from it.
analogy: Turning a whole book into a unique 64-character serial number; changing even a single comma in the book produces a completely different serial number.
keyTakeaway: Used to verify file integrity and safely store password verifiers without saving plaintext passwords.

formalDefinition: The practice of appending a unique, cryptographically random string (salt) to each user's password before hashing, defending against precomputed rainbow table attacks.
eli5: Adding a random secret pinch of spice to each user's password before scrambling it, so even if two people pick '123456', their stored fingerprints look completely different.
analogy: Giving every locker at a gym a different random prefix code before scrambling it, so a stolen master list of common passwords becomes useless.
keyTakeaway: Essential defense in modern authentication systems alongside slow hashing algorithms like Argon2 or bcrypt.

formalDefinition: A code injection vulnerability in which untrusted user input is concatenated directly into a database query, allowing attackers to manipulate SQL syntax and read or alter unauthorized data.
eli5: Tricking a website's search box by typing database commands instead of a normal name, causing the database to obey your hidden instructions.
analogy: Writing '1000 dollars AND give me the keys to the vault' on a bank deposit slip when the clerk blindly reads every word aloud as an official order.
keyTakeaway: Always prevented by using parameterized queries (prepared statements) rather than string concatenation.

formalDefinition: A mathematical formula for determining conditional probability, describing how to update the probability of a hypothesis given new observed evidence: P(A|B) = P(B|A)P(A) / P(B).
eli5: Updating how likely you think something is after you see a new clue, while remembering how rare that thing was to begin with.
analogy: If you hear barking outside, you might think it's a dog. If you live next to a zoo with seals that bark, you update your guess based on both the sound and how common dogs vs. seals are in your neighborhood.
keyTakeaway: Drives spam filters, medical diagnostics, and probabilistic machine learning models.

formalDefinition: For a linear transformation represented by a matrix A, an eigenvector is a nonzero vector whose direction remains unchanged after transformation, scaled only by a scalar factor called its eigenvalue.
eli5: Special arrows inside a stretching or rotating transformation that keep pointing in the exact same direction—they only grow longer or shorter.
analogy: When you stretch a rubber sheet evenly from left to right, arrows drawn horizontally stay horizontal (eigenvectors) and just get longer by the stretch factor (eigenvalue).
keyTakeaway: Essential for Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Google PageRank, and dimensionality reduction in AI.

formalDefinition: A stochastic model describing a sequence of possible events in which the probability of each event depends solely on the state attained in the previous event (the memoryless property).
eli5: A system that predicts what happens next using only where you are right now, completely forgetting how you got there.
analogy: Playing a board game where your next possible squares depend only on the space your piece is currently sitting on, not on the last 10 rolls you made.
keyTakeaway: Used in autocomplete keyboards, weather modeling, reinforcement learning, and web page ranking.

formalDefinition: The problem of determining whether there exists an assignment of True/False truth values to variables that makes a given Boolean formula evaluate to True; the first problem proven to be NP-complete.
eli5: Figuring out whether there is any combination of light switches (ON or OFF) that satisfies a giant list of strict rules all at once.
analogy: Planning a dinner seating chart with 50 guests where 'Alice won't sit next to Bob' and 'Carol must sit near Dave'—checking if any valid seating arrangement even exists.
keyTakeaway: Modern SAT solvers power hardware chip verification, automated scheduling, and software bug-finding.

formalDefinition: A system of arithmetic for integers where numbers wrap around upon reaching a fixed positive value called the modulus, denoted a ≡ b (mod n).
eli5: Math that wraps around in a circle, just like a 12-hour clock where 3 hours after 10 o'clock is 1 o'clock instead of 13.
analogy: If today is Friday and you count 10 days forward, you wrap around the 7-day week and land on Monday (10 mod 7 = 3 days past Friday).
keyTakeaway: Forms the mathematical backbone of hash tables, checksums, and modern public-key cryptography.
